claims.claim: In mid-market AP, invoices wait a median of 9.4 days for an approver versus 1.6 days in data entry, so approval routing is the bottleneck.
claims.quote: invoices spend a median of 9.4 days waiting for an approver and 1.6 days in data entry

claims.claim: Match exceptions are 18% of invoice volume but consume 61% of AP staff hours.
claims.quote: Invoices that fail a match against the purchase order or receipt make up 18% of volume but 61% of accounts-payable staff hours

claims.claim: Exceptions are resolved over email, leaving no auditor-visible record of the reasoning behind each resolution.
claims.quote: Exceptions are resolved over email, so the reasoning behind each resolution is not recorded anywhere an auditor can see.

claims.claim: Fully loaded cost per invoice is $9 to $14 with ERP-native AP modules versus $15 to $22 for fully manual teams.
claims.quote: Fully loaded processing cost sits between $9 and $14 per invoice for companies that have adopted ERP-native AP modules, against $15 to $22 for fully manual teams

claims.claim: 41% of surveyed controllers say their auditors added payment-control testing in the last two years.
claims.quote: 41% of controllers surveyed said their auditors had added testing on payment controls in the last two years

claims.claim: ERP-native AP modules are weak at approval routing and exception handling, treating them as a simple linear workflow.
claims.quote: Their weakness is approval routing and exception handling, which they treat as a simple linear workflow.

claims.claim: Buyers of outsourced AP report losing visibility into exceptions and approvals and slower supplier-dispute response.
claims.quote: Buyers report losing visibility into exceptions and approvals, and a slower response when a supplier disputes a payment.

claims.claim: The status quo of spreadsheets, shared inbox and email approvals remains the most common competitor because switching requires IT time for ERP integration.
claims.quote: Still the most common competitor, because switching requires finance to win time from IT for the ERP integration.
claims.alternative: Spreadsheets, shared inbox and email approvals

claims.claim: After adopting the Contoso AP module, a manufacturer's capture worked but invoices still sat waiting for approval.
claims.quote: the invoices get into the system fine now. They just sit there.

claims.claim: Plant managers batch-approve accumulated invoices without reviewing them.
claims.quote: A plant manager has forty invoices waiting and approves them on a Friday afternoon, in a batch, without looking.

claims.claim: A manufacturer's month-end close slipped from day 6 to day 9 over a year, attributed to late approvals.
claims.quote: Month-end close slipped from day 6 to day 9 over the last year.

claims.claim: An audit found a $38,000 duplicate payment that passed as a resolved exception, with no record of who approved the override.
claims.quote: Last year's audit found a duplicate payment of $38,000 that had gone through as a resolved exception. Nobody could say who approved the override.

claims.claim: PO-receipt mismatches are chased through chains of email between AP, plants and suppliers that drag on for weeks.
claims.quote: When a receipt doesn't match the PO we email the plant, the plant emails the supplier, and three weeks later someone remembers.

claims.claim: The Contoso AP module supports only one approver per cost center and no escalation.
claims.quote: the module supports one approver per cost center and no escalation

claims.claim: A controller rejected outsourcing because the provider would not know the plants well enough to resolve exceptions.
claims.quote: I'm not handing my exceptions to someone who doesn't know our plants.

claims.claim: A controller says they would evaluate a dedicated approval layer only if it does not require replacing the ERP.
claims.quote: Would evaluate a dedicated approval layer if it did not mean replacing the ERP

claims.claim: The controller's need is faster approvals, not faster capture.
claims.quote: I don't need faster capture. I need the approvals to happen.

claims.claim: Controllers want to answer an auditor by clicking an invoice and seeing who decided to pay it and why.
claims.quote: If an auditor asks why we paid an invoice, I want to click on it and see who decided and why.

claims.claim: A clinic group outsourced AP to Fabrikam in 2023 and brought it back in house in early 2026.
claims.quote: The group outsourced accounts payable to Fabrikam Payables Services in 2023 and brought it back in house in early 2026.

claims.claim: Under outsourcing, mismatched invoices came back to the in-house team late and without context.
claims.quote: Everything that didn't match came back to us anyway, except now it came back late and without context.

claims.claim: The clinic AP team tracks open exceptions in a spreadsheet of roughly 300 rows.
claims.quote: the team keeps a spreadsheet of open exceptions that runs to roughly 300 rows at any time

claims.claim: Two of six AP specialists left in a year, and exception history held in their inboxes left with them.
claims.quote: Two of six AP specialists left in the last year.

claims.claim: A fake supplier bank-detail change was caught only by chance because there is no formal verification step.
claims.quote: It was caught because a specialist happened to call the supplier. There is no formal verification step.

claims.claim: The clinic group's ERP AP module cannot route approvals to clinic managers who are not ERP users.
claims.quote: the group's ERP has an AP module but it does not route to clinic managers who are not ERP users

claims.claim: Outsourcing was cheaper per invoice on paper but cost more once exceptions were counted.
claims.quote: Cheaper per invoice on paper. It cost us more in exceptions.

claims.claim: The AP manager wants approvals non-ERP clinic managers can complete without a login, plus a record of every exception decision.
claims.quote: Wants approvals that clinic managers can complete without an ERP login, and a record of every exception decision.

claims.claim: A pre-IPO CFO frames AP as a controls problem: avoiding a material weakness in payment controls.
claims.quote: What I can't have is a material weakness in payment controls the year we file.

claims.claim: With approvals in email and Slack, reconstructing who approved a payment took about 40 minutes per invoice across 60 audit samples.
claims.quote: Today approvals happen in email and Slack. Reconstructing who approved a given payment takes the controller about 40 minutes per invoice sampled, and the auditors sampled 60.

claims.claim: A software company's vendor bank-change fraud attempt was stopped only because of an unusual amount and a controller's question.
claims.quote: It was stopped only because the amount was unusually large and the controller asked a question.

claims.claim: The CFO's objection to the already-licensed Contoso AP module is that approval policies cannot vary by amount and department.
claims.quote: The CFO's concern is that approval policies cannot vary by amount and department.

claims.claim: The CFO says they would fund a tool that avoids hiring a third AP specialist, estimated at $95,000 fully loaded.
claims.quote: would fund a tool if it removed the need to hire a third AP specialist, estimated at $95,000 fully loaded

claims.claim: The CFO names an approval trail and bank-change verification as the proof needed to sign.
claims.quote: Show me the approval trail and the bank-change verification, and I'll sign this quarter.

claims.claim: The CFO says they are buying evidence, not automation.
claims.quote: I'm not buying automation. I'm buying evidence.

claims.claim: Four of five wins were against the Contoso AP module at existing Contoso customers, decided by multi-level routing with escalation and approvals for non-ERP users.
claims.quote: Four of five wins were against the Contoso Finance Suite AP module, where the buyer already owned Contoso. The deciding factor in each was multi-level approval routing with escalation, and approvals that non-ERP users could complete from email or mobile.

claims.claim: Three wins cited the exception audit trail during procurement, typically after the controller showed it to their auditor.
claims.quote: Three wins cited the exception audit trail during the procurement stage, typically after the controller showed it to their auditor.

claims.claim: Deals with a pilot closed at 5 of 6 while deals without a pilot closed at 0 of 6.
claims.quote: Deals with a pilot closed at 5 of 6; deals without a pilot closed at 0 of 6.

claims.claim: Every loss to the status quo stalled waiting for IT to schedule the ERP integration.
claims.quote: In each case the project stalled waiting for IT to schedule the ERP integration.
claims.alternative: Spreadsheets, shared inbox and email approvals

claims.claim: Both losses to Fabrikam were buyers above 12,000 invoices a month who chose on cost per invoice without a pilot.
claims.quote: Both buyers had more than 12,000 invoices a month and chose on cost per invoice. Neither ran a pilot.

claims.claim: One deal was lost to Contoso because the buyer's IT refused a second system touching the ERP.
claims.quote: The buyer's IT team refused a second system touching the ERP.

claims.claim: Buyers asked for a read-only ERP connection first, with write-back later, to reduce integration effort.
claims.quote: Buyers asked for a read-only ERP connection first, with write-back later.

claims.claim: Payment-redirection fraud now accounts for the largest share of reported losses among mid-sized companies, per audit firms.
claims.quote: Payment-redirection fraud, in which a criminal impersonates a supplier and asks for bank details to be changed, now accounts for the largest share of reported losses among mid-sized companies

claims.claim: Auditors increasingly ask whether companies can show who approved each payment and whether that person was authorized for the amount.
claims.quote: can the company show who approved each payment, and was that person authorized for the amount?

claims.claim: An audit partner says most mid-sized companies have an approval process but very few can prove it.
claims.quote: Most of these companies have an approval process. Very few can prove it

claims.claim: One controller estimated reconstructing approval evidence costs two weeks of a senior accountant's time per audit.
claims.quote: One estimated it at two weeks of a senior accountant's time per audit.

claims.claim: After turning on the ERP AP module, a distribution AP lead still spends Mondays chasing department heads who ignore approval notifications.
claims.quote: department heads ignore the notifications, and I spend Mondays chasing people on chat

claims.claim: A nonprofit controller built spreadsheet-macro reminder emails because the ERP module routes to one approver with no escalation or delegation.
claims.quote: The module routes to one approver and stops. No escalation, no delegation when someone is on leave. We built reminder emails in a spreadsheet macro.

claims.claim: Each PO mismatch becomes a 10-email thread, and audit questions are answered by searching an inbox.
claims.quote: Every PO mismatch turns into a 10-email thread. When an auditor asks about one, I search my inbox.

claims.claim: A logistics AP manager found outsourcing savings mostly disappeared because exceptions still came back in house.
claims.quote: Their per-invoice price was good, but exceptions still came back to us, so the savings mostly disappeared.

claims.claim: Replacing ERP payables with a standalone AP suite took eight months of migration and left lasting IT resistance.
claims.quote: The migration took eight months and IT still talks about it.
claims.alternative: Standalone AP suite replacing ERP payables

claims.claim: A sponsored vendor post claims customers see up to 90% faster processing and 80% lower costs.
claims.quote: Our customers see up to 90% faster processing and 80% lower costs.

claims.claim: A sponsored vendor post asserts touchless processing is now the standard.
claims.quote: Touchless processing is now the standard, and companies that wait will fall behind.
